topic: The seven things on which khums is obligatory
states: Lists the seven categories: surplus income from earnings and gains, mined products, treasure, lawful property mixed with unlawful property, gems from diving, spoils of war, and (per the majority opinion) land a dhimmi buys from a Muslim.
precaution: FATWA (the seventh per the majority opinion)

topic: Earnings from trade, crafts or any work
states: Property gained by any kind of earning (including wages for prayers or fasts performed for the dead) owes one-fifth of what exceeds the year's living expenses of the person and family.
conditions: Only the part above the year's living expenses

topic: Gains not earned (e.g. gifts)
states: Property obtained without earning, such as a gift, owes khums if it exceeds the year's living expenses, except the cases of ruling 1771.
issues: Whether a gift in kind kept and used counts as spent on the year's needs is not stated here (see 1792–1800).

topic: Mahr, khul' payment, diyah and inheritance
states: No khums on mahr received, on what a husband receives for a khul' divorce, on diyah, or on inheritance received under valid inheritance laws. Inheritance by another way (e.g. ta'sib) is a gain. Unexpected inheritance from someone other than father or son owes khums if above the year's expenses, by obligatory precaution.
conditions: Valid inheritance law vs another way
Unexpected, and not from father or son
precaution: MIXED (fatwa; obligatory precaution for unexpected inheritance)

topic: Inheritance on which the deceased did not pay khums
states: If the heir knows the deceased did not pay khums on the inherited property, the heir pays it; khums the deceased owed on other property is paid from the estate. Not required when the deceased did not believe in or never paid khums and did not will its payment.
conditions: The heir knows khums was unpaid
exceptions: Deceased did not believe in khums or never paid it, and left no will to pay it
issues: Which value of the property (at death, on receipt, now) the one-fifth is taken on is not stated.

topic: Savings from frugality
states: Money saved by spending frugally still owes khums.

topic: Living expenses paid by someone else
states: If someone else pays all of a person's living expenses, khums is due on the person's entire earnings.
conditions: All expenses are paid by another
issues: Partial support is not addressed.

topic: Income from a private endowment (waqf) given to particular persons
states: Crops, fruit or rent earned from property endowed to particular persons owe khums on what exceeds their year's living expenses.
issues: General endowments are not covered here.

topic: Charity received by a poor person
states: Obligatory or recommended charity received, or profit from it, that exceeds the year's expenses owes khums by obligatory precaution. Property received as khums or zakat by someone entitled owes no khums itself, but its profit above the year's expenses does.
exceptions: Khums or zakat received by an entitled person (the property itself)

topic: Buying with the very money on which khums is unpaid
states: Buying with specified untaxed money from a Twelver Shia seller is valid; the purchased item becomes liable for khums; no jurist's permission needed.
conditions: The purchase is made with that specific money

workflows.firstTime: relevant (items bought from unpaid income) but not named

issues: The amount due on the item (its price paid or current value) is not stated here.

topic: Buying on credit and paying with untaxed money
states: The sale is valid but the buyer owes the khums on the untaxed money paid.
conditions: Bought on credit, paid later with untaxed money
issues: Amount owed = one-fifth of the untaxed money paid; how this enters a first-time assessment is not stated.

topic: Buying an item on which khums was not paid
states: When a Twelver Shia buys something on which khums was unpaid, the seller owes the khums, not the buyer.

topic: Receiving a gift on which khums was not paid
states: The giver owes the unpaid khums, not the recipient; but the gift itself is a gain for the recipient under ruling 1770 if it exceeds the year's expenses.

topic: Property from someone who does not pay khums
states: Property acquired from a non-Muslim or from someone who does not believe in or pay khums does not owe that person's khums.
issues: The recipient's own gain is still governed by 1769–1770.

topic: When the khums year starts
states: Someone who trades or works pays khums one year after starting, on what exceeds the year's expenses (also seasonal earners whose income covers a significant part of their expenses). Someone without an occupation, or with incidental profit, counts a year from each profit and may keep a separate year for each amount.

workflows.firstTime: named implicitly: the first year starts when work starts

issues: Separate yearly cycles per profit need date logic the engine lacks.

topic: Paying during the year; solar year
states: Khums may be paid whenever profit is gained or delayed to year end; if the person knows he will not need it, paying at once is obligatory precaution. A solar year may be used.
conditions: Knows the profit will not be needed before year end

topic: Death during the year
states: Living expenses until death are deducted, then khums is paid on the rest at once.
issues: The calculator assesses living persons; out of scope unless an estate workflow is added.

topic: Business stock price rise reversed within the year
states: If unsold business stock rose and fell back within the same year (not above cost), no khums on the rise.
conditions: Price falls back within the year
issues: Needs year-end market value input.

topic: Business stock held past year end hoping for a rise
states: If stock that rose is held past the year end and its price then falls, khums on the rise is obligatory precaution.
conditions: Held in hope of a higher price

workflows.missedYear: relevant across years but not named

issues: Needs year-end value; valuation capability missing.

topic: Non-business property that rises in value and is sold
states: For non-business property on which khums was paid, the price increase realised on sale owes khums if above the year's expenses; likewise fruit or growth of animals.

topic: Garden created to sell later
states: Fruit, tree growth, usable pruned branches and price increase are liable when the garden is meant for sale; if meant for the fruit, the price increase is not.
conditions: Intention: sell the garden vs sell the fruit
issues: Agricultural valuation is outside the calculator's inputs.

topic: Trees grown for wood
states: Khums every year on their growth; pruned branches sold above the year's expenses.
issues: Valuation of growth is outside the calculator's inputs.

topic: Several lines of business
states: Same kind of business with shared accounts: profit and loss offset. Different kinds of business, or one line with separate accounts: no offset, by obligatory precaution.
precaution: MIXED (fatwa; obligatory precaution for no offset)

topic: Costs of earning
states: Expenses of making the profit (brokerage, transport) and damage to tools are deducted from profit.

topic: Living expenses spent from the year's profit
states: What is spent during the year on food, clothing, furniture, a house, a son's wedding, a daughter's trousseau, ziyarah and similar is not liable, if within the person's status.
issues: 'Within status' is a judgement of the person's circumstances: asked as a confirmation, never judged by AI.

topic: Vows, kaffarah and gifts given
states: Spending on vows and kaffarah, and gifts or prizes given within status, count as living expenses.

topic: Daughter's trousseau acquired gradually
states: Where custom is to gather a trousseau over years and not doing so is beneath one's status, a portion bought from the year's profit, within status and commonly part of that year's spending, is not liable. Beyond status, or bought next year from this year's profit, it is liable.
conditions: Bought within the same year from that year's profit
issues: Custom and status are judgements of the person's circumstances: asked, never judged.

topic: Hajj and ziyarah costs; journey spanning two years
states: Hajj and ziyarah costs are living expenses of the year; what is spent in the following year from the previous year's profit owes khums.
conditions: Spent in the same khums year

workflows.missedYear: relevant (spending crossing years) but not named

topic: Expenses counted only against profit
states: Someone with profit who also owns other property not liable for khums may count the year's expenses against the profit alone.
conditions: Owns other property not liable for khums

topic: Provisions left over at year end
states: Provisions bought from the year's profit and surplus to needs at year end owe khums; if paying their value and the price rose, the year-end price is used.
conditions: Surplus to needs at year end
issues: Needs a year-end value input for left-over provisions.

topic: Furniture and items bought from profit
states: Household items bought from profit and used before year end owe nothing even if no longer needed later. Items usually kept for later years (e.g. seasonal clothes) owe nothing even if unused. Other items not needed at all during the year owe khums by obligatory precaution. Jewellery a woman no longer wears is not liable.
conditions: Used within the year, or customarily kept for later years
precaution: MIXED (fatwa; obligatory precaution for unused items)

topic: No profit in a year
states: A year's expenses cannot be deducted from the next year's profit when the year had no profit.

workflows.missedYear: named across years (no carry-forward of expenses)

topic: Spending from capital before profit in the same year
states: If one spends from capital early in a year and makes profit before year end, the amount taken from capital may be deducted from that profit.

topic: Loss of business capital
states: Capital lost in business may be deducted from profit of the same year.

topic: Replacing lost property needed in the year
states: If non-capital property is lost and needed in the same year, replacing it from that year's profit is not liable.

topic: Loans for living expenses or a needed house or car
states: A loan taken in a year without profit for living expenses cannot be deducted from later years' profit, though repaying it from later income is not liable. A loan for a needed item (house, car) in use may be deducted from future income while owed and not already deducted. A loan for living expenses in a year that later shows profit is deducted from that profit. Office note: outstanding balance deductible until cumulative surplus reaches it, then only interest.
conditions: Item in personal use while owed

workflows.missedYear: named across years (deduction from future years)

issues: Tracking the balance already deducted across years needs carry-over the engine lacks.

topic: Loans to grow wealth or buy unneeded things
states: If such a loan is repaid from the year's profit without paying khums, khums is due at year end on the borrowed money or the item bought, unless it perished during the year.
exceptions: The money or item perished during the year

topic: Paying khums in kind or by value
states: Khums may be paid from the item itself or its monetary value; paying with another item is problematic (obligatory precaution) without a jurist's permission.
issues: Payment method, not calculation.

topic: Disposal before paying overdue khums
states: Once property is liable and a year has passed, the owner may not dispose of it until khums is paid.

topic: Treating owed khums as a debt while using the wealth
states: Someone owing khums cannot simply treat it as a debt and use all the wealth; if the wealth is used and lost, the khums remains due.

topic: Settlement (exchange) with a qualified jurist
states: After an exchange settlement with a qualified jurist, the person may use all property and keeps later profit, but must repay the debt gradually without negligence.
issues: A settlement is an arrangement with a jurist: the calculator records it and stops, never computes it.

topic: Partner whose capital has unpaid khums
states: A Twelver Shia partner who paid khums may use joint property even if the other partner contributes capital with unpaid khums.

topic: Profit of a minor
states: A minor's profit (even gifts) not used for the child's expenses during the year is liable; the guardian pays it, otherwise the child after maturity. Exception for a discerning child following a jurist who holds no khums on a minor's property.
conditions: Not used for the child's expenses during the year
exceptions: Discerning child following a jurist who holds no khums for minors
issues: The calculator assesses one adult; minors' property is out of scope.

topic: Doubt whether a former owner paid khums
states: A new owner who doubts whether the former owner paid may use the property; even if sure it was unpaid, a Twelver Shia may use it when the former owner is someone who does not pay khums.

topic: Item bought from profit that is not a reasonable expense
states: Such an item owes khums at year end; if unpaid and its value rises, khums is on its current value.
conditions: Not a necessary or reasonable expense for one's status

workflows.missedYear: named implicitly (value rises after unpaid year end)

issues: Needs current-value input.

topic: Item bought with money whose khums year passed unpaid
states: Bought on an unspecified undertaking and not as an investment: khums on the purchase price. Bought with the specific untaxed money: khums on the item's current value.
conditions: Kind of purchase (unspecified undertaking vs specified money)
Bought as an investment or not
issues: The investment case (bought to sell when the price rises) is not stated: stop for review.
Needs purchase price, purchase kind and current value inputs.

topic: Someone who never paid, or missed years
states: For someone who never paid since maturity, or missed years: unneeded items bought from trading profit owe khums once a year has passed since trading began (non-traders: since the profit). Household items needed within status owe nothing if the person knows they were bought in the year of profit, with that year's profit, and used that year. If unknown, settlement with a qualified jurist proportionate to the probability is obligatory precaution (e.g. 50% probable → khums on 50%).
conditions: Bought in the year of profit, with that year's profit, used that year (known)
exceptions: Needed household items meeting the three conditions
precaution: MIXED (fatwa; obligatory precaution for settlement when unknown)

workflows.missedYear: named (unpaid for a number of years)

issues: The proportion of probability is the person's own estimate made with a jurist; the calculator stops and refers rather than applying a percentage.

topic: Mined products: ownership and liability
states: Extracted mined products may be owned if there is no legal obstacle; khums is due when their value reaches the nisab.

topic: Nisab for mined products
states: Nisab is 15 common mithqal of coined gold (office note: 69.12 g), measured after extraction costs; later costs such as refining are then deducted and khums paid on the rest.
conditions: Value after extraction costs reaches 69.12 g of coined gold
issues: Needs the value of 69.12 g of coined gold in the person's currency (user input on a date); threshold capability missing.

topic: Mined product below the nisab
states: Below the nisab, it is liable only as part of profits exceeding the year's living expenses.
issues: Below-nisab amount moves into annual surplus: needs threshold capability.

topic: Chalk and lime
states: By obligatory precaution treated as mined products: khums when value reaches the nisab, without deducting living expenses.
issues: Needs threshold capability.

topic: Location of the mine
states: Khums applies whether the mine is above or below ground, on one's own land or ownerless land.

topic: Unknown whether the nisab is reached
states: Must establish the value if possible (obligatory precaution); if impossible, khums is not obligatory.
issues: An unknown value stops for clarification, never assumed.

topic: Joint extraction
states: If the total reaches the nisab but no individual share does, it is not liable.
issues: Needs the person's own share and threshold capability.

topic: Extraction under another's land without consent
states: Disputed ownership; settlement by obligatory precaution, otherwise a jurist decides.

topic: Definition of treasure trove
states: Movable concealed property not within people's reach, hidden abnormally underground, in a tree, mountain or wall.

topic: Treasure on ownerless land
states: The finder may take it and must pay khums.

topic: Nisab for treasure
states: Khums becomes obligatory when the value equals 105 mithqal of coined silver or 15 mithqal of coined gold.
issues: Needs silver and gold values on the date; threshold capability missing.

topic: Treasure on purchased or rented land
states: After informing previous owners who may claim it, the finder may keep it and pay khums.
issues: Whether previous owners were informed is asked, never assumed.

topic: Several treasures
states: Totals are combined; found at different times, combined if the interval is short, otherwise each counted separately.
issues: 'Long interval' is not quantified: stop for review.

topic: Treasure found by two people
states: Not liable if neither share reaches the nisab.

topic: Property found in an animal's stomach
states: After informing possible owners, khums if it reaches the treasure nisab; even below it by obligatory precaution.

topic: Mixed wealth: unknown owner and unknown amount
states: When lawful and unlawful property are inseparable, with unknown owner and amount (not known to be more or less than a fifth), paying khums makes it lawful; by obligatory precaution to someone entitled to both khums and radd al-mazalim.

topic: Mixed wealth: known amount, unknown owner
states: Give that amount as sadaqah on the owner's behalf; obligatory precaution to get a jurist's permission first.
issues: Not khums: the calculator stops and refers.

topic: Mixed wealth: unknown amount, known owner
states: Without agreement, give what is certainly the owner's; if at fault in mixing, more than the probable amount by obligatory precaution.

topic: Unlawful part later found larger than a fifth
states: The excess known beyond khums is given as sadaqah for the owner.

topic: Owner found after khums or sadaqah
states: If the owner does not agree, reimburse his share by obligatory precaution.

topic: Owner is one of a known group
states: Inform all; disputes go to settlement or a jurist; otherwise drawing lots.

topic: Gems from diving and their nisab
states: Pearls, coral or other gems brought up by diving owe khums if worth 18 nukhud of gold (office note: 3.456 g), combining dives without a long interval; separate seasons and individual shares below the nisab are not liable.
issues: Needs the value of 3.456 g of gold on the date; threshold capability missing.
'Long interval' is given only by example (different seasons).

topic: Sea gems obtained without diving
states: By obligatory precaution liable; from the surface or shore, liable only as profit above the year's expenses.

topic: Fish caught without diving
states: Liable only as profit above the year's living expenses.

topic: Gem found incidentally while diving
states: Liable if kept; by obligatory precaution in any case.

topic: Gem inside a sea creature
states: Natural container (like an oyster): liable if it reaches the nisab; swallowed incidentally: liable even below the nisab by obligatory precaution.

topic: Gems from big rivers
states: Diving in big rivers (e.g. Tigris, Euphrates) for gems is liable.

topic: Ambergris
states: Liable at 18 nukhud of gold or more, by diving or from the surface or shore.
issues: Needs threshold capability.

topic: Professional divers and miners
states: Items on which khums was paid as mined or dived products are not liable again as annual surplus.

topic: Minors who mine, find treasure or dive
states: The guardian pays; otherwise the child after maturity.
issues: Out of scope (minors).

topic: Spoils of war
states: Not relevant to individual assessment.

topic: Spoils of war without the Imam's authorisation
states: Not relevant to individual assessment.

topic: Spoils rules and inviolable property
states: Not relevant to individual assessment.

topic: Taking property from a harbi disbeliever
states: Not relevant to individual assessment.

topic: Property of a nasibi
states: Not relevant to individual assessment.

topic: Land a dhimmi buys from a Muslim
states: Not relevant to the calculator's users.

topic: Two halves of khums
states: Khums is divided into the sayyids' share (to poor, orphan or stranded sayyids) and the Imam's share (to a qualified jurist or as he authorises; obligatory precaution: the most learned marja aware of public affairs).

topic: Orphan and stranded sayyids
states: An orphan sayyid must be poor; a stranded traveller may receive it even if not poor at home.

topic: Journey for a sinful purpose
states: Not given, by obligatory precaution.

topic: Sayyid who is not 'adil; not Twelver
states: May be given to one not 'adil; not to one who is not a Twelver Shia.

topic: Sayyid who uses it for sin
states: Not given; obligatory precaution also for those it helps to sin or who openly sin.

topic: Proof of being a sayyid
states: Two 'adil witnesses, or certainty or confidence.

topic: Known as a sayyid in his home town
states: May be given unless certain or confident otherwise.

topic: Wife who is a sayyidah
states: Not for her obligatory maintenance (obligatory precaution); allowed for dependants she cannot support.

topic: Dependants who are sayyids
states: Not for their obligatory maintenance (obligatory precaution); allowed for other needs.

topic: Poor sayyid not supported by his provider
states: May be given.

topic: Limit per recipient
states: Not more than a year's expenses at once (obligatory precaution); never beyond that in instalments.

topic: Taking khums to another town
states: Allowed; the payer bears loss and cannot deduct transport costs from khums.
issues: Transport costs are not deducted from khums.

topic: Receiving as a jurist's agent
states: Taking possession as the jurist's agent discharges the duty.

topic: Overvaluing items given as khums
states: Not allowed; items other than money need a jurist's authorisation (obligatory precaution).

topic: Offsetting a debt owed by a sayyid
states: Needs a jurist's permission or a give-and-return, by obligatory precaution; never against the Imam's share for a poor debtor, with stated exceptions.
issues: Debt offsetting is not a calculation step.

topic: No condition of return
states: The payer may not require the recipient to return it.
